chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man whose father did not sacrifice an animal for him until he grew up, becoming a young boy or a man who had reached maturity. He said: 'If a sacrifice is made on his behalf, or the son sacrifices for himself, it suffices for his Aqiqa.'
And he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The child is held in pledge by his Aqiqa; his parents ransom him or leave him in pledge.'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: Sufficed/Valid: The act fulfilled the religious obligation.
key_terms.ضُحِّيَ: Sacrificed (passive): An animal was sacrificed on behalf of someone.
key_terms.عَقِيقَة: Aqiqa: The ritual sacrifice of an animal performed on behalf of a newborn child.
key_terms.فَكَّهُ: He ransomed him: He freed him from the pledge.
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ: Held in pledge/Liened: A state of being held accountable or bound until a condition is met.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father does not sacrifice an animal for his son's Aqiqa before the son grows up?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of deferred Aqiqa, establishing that if the father neglected the ritual, the son may perform it for himself upon reaching maturity, thereby fulfilling the spiritual 'pledge' mentioned in the Prophet's saying. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of this Sunnah, ensuring that the child is not deprived of its spiritual benefits due to parental oversight.
